answer: Copper-financed bridge deposits require each identity to lock a unique asset class, making cloning nonviable as the marginal clone faces a guaranteed loss from tying up incompatible currencies. Jetty verification enforces usage across disparate systems, so attackers must acquire platform-specific credentials with no transfer value between them, trapping clones in isolated domains. The mechanism, Cross-Platform Identity Lock, mandates that creating a new identity demands irreversible allocation of a verifiable resource whose value decays with each duplicate claim.
